input.step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Inventory: there are 10 drawn entities. All are kept. META MANAGER runs on EKS as a microservice architecture. The MetaStore (Elasticsearch plus Neo4j, a combination of document and graph database) uses OpenSearch. The S3 data lake, Kafka (ThirdParty) and EMR sit inside the data lake box. RDS and Vertica (ThirdParty) are the consumption stores. Multiple Data Sources are drawn as a database icon (service kept as RDS, as in the world model). Applications are ThirdParty. DA/DS (UserCompanyAnalyst) is kept as a specific consumer role, not a generic actor. Nothing is fused or expanded, and no infrastructure-as-code or DevOps layer is added because none is drawn as a runtime component.
2. Ledger: there are 8 visual_connections entries. Each one becomes an edge in the same direction. Three entries are marked 'both' (Multiple Data Sources<->Kafka, Applications<->EMR, EMR<->S3), so each of these gives two edges, one per direction. That makes 11 ledger edges.
3. Edges added from the audio: (a) Multiple Data Sources -> Meta Manager, from 'we need to discover which tables, schemas, APIs you have... we get all of this data into MetaManager'. The whiteboard also shows a pink line from the sources up to Meta Manager. (b) RDS -> DA/DS and (c) Vertica -> DA/DS, from 'data analyst and data scientist are going to consume this data'.
4. Flows: flow 0 is metadata discovery and indexing. Flow 1 is collection through Kafka, orchestrated by Meta Manager. Flow 2 is collection and processing through EMR. Flow 3 is consumption through RDS, Vertica and DA/DS. Flow 4 is connecting data back to business applications and sources through the enterprise streaming platform.
5. Self-check: 8 visual_connections entries; 14 edges emitted (11 from the ledger plus 3 from the audio). 14 >= 8.

graph.name: Majid Al Futtaim - 'The Grid' Enterprise Data Platform (Collect, Protect, Connect)
graph.categories: Data Lake, Analytics, Streaming, Metadata Management, Customer 360
graph.notes: Data platform built around three goals: collect, protect and connect data across 14 countries and several business units (retail, real estate, malls, entertainment). The infrastructure is defined as code by the DevOps team and can be spun up and down on demand (for example, for IT tests). The MVP reached production in 6 months. Business result: a 360-degree customer view across Vox Cinemas and Carrefour, which enables cross-brand marketing campaigns and push notifications.

nodes.name: META MANAGER
nodes.notes: The 'brains' of the grid. A microservice architecture on EKS that a frontend (F.E.) connects to. It hides the complexity of the data movement technology, discovers tables, schemas and APIs, orchestrates data movement, and applies data protection to data coming into and out of the data lake.

nodes.name: ELASTICSEARCH NEO4J (MetaStore)
nodes.notes: MetaStore that combines a document database (Elasticsearch) and a graph database (Neo4j). Stores and indexes the discovered metadata.

nodes.name: S3 DATA LAKE
nodes.notes: Central data lake holding all collected data, about 60 TB today.

nodes.name: KAFKA
nodes.notes: Enterprise streaming platform shared across all MAF companies. 600 topics, 250 GB, 7-day average retention. Streams data from distributed sources (different networks, countries and technologies) into the data lake.

nodes.name: EMR
nodes.notes: Used together with Kafka to bring data into the data lake. Processes data and exchanges it with applications and APIs.

nodes.name: RDS
nodes.notes: Consumption data store. Data can be published or consumed through APIs or OLTP.

nodes.name: VERTICA
nodes.notes: Analytics data store used by data analysts and data scientists for traditional analytics.

nodes.name: MULTIPLE DATA SOURCES
nodes.notes: Distributed source databases across different networks, countries and technologies.

nodes.name: APPLICATIONS
nodes.notes: Business applications and APIs (for example, the loyalty app). Data is consumed from them and sent back to the business to connect with customers (push notifications, cross campaigns).

nodes.name: DA/DS
nodes.notes: Data analysts and data scientists who consume data, run models and build dashboards.

edges.notes: Meta Manager discovers tables, schemas and APIs from the data sources (supported by the audio and the pink line on the whiteboard).
Discovered metadata is stored and indexed in the MetaStore (document and graph database).
Meta Manager orchestrates data movement through the Kafka streaming platform.
Data is collected from multiple sources across networks and countries into Kafka (600 topics, 250 GB).
Reverse direction of the bidirectional arrow: the enterprise streaming platform sends data back to the sources and the business.
Kafka streams data into the S3 data lake (7-day retention in Kafka).
Data from applications and APIs is ingested by EMR.
Processed data is sent back to the business applications to connect with customers (for example, loyalty app push notifications).
EMR writes data into the S3 data lake (about 60 TB).
EMR reads data from the S3 data lake for processing.
Protected data from the data lake is sent to RDS for consumption through APIs or OLTP.
Data is sent to Vertica for analytics.
Data analysts and data scientists consume data (supported by the audio).
Data analysts and data scientists run models and build dashboards on Vertica (supported by the audio).
